source.title: TAIA: Large Language Models are Out-of-Distribution Data Learners
source.authors: Shu-Yang Jiang; Yusheng Liao; Ya Zhang; Yu Wang; Yan-Feng Wang

record.tranche_reason: The authors follow the cited red-teaming procedure and evaluate harmful-request attack success on AdvBench after fine-tuning, including a vanilla fine-tuning comparison.
record.gate_note: Table 5 reports attack-success rates for three fine-tuning conditions; Figures 6–8 give separate illustrative outputs for harmful, identity-shifting, and benign tuning. Other fine-tuning and benchmark results do not measure the claim versions. AlpacaEval helpfulness results are not included as rows because they do not measure harmful compliance.
record.test_reason: Section 5 (RQ2) follows Qi et al.'s red-teaming recipe on LLaMA2-7B-chat. It reports AdvBench attack success after vanilla fine-tuning on 100 harmful, 10 identity-shifting and benign Alpaca-GPT4 samples, against the untuned model at 0.00. The vanilla results bear on V1 and V2 directly. The paper is mainly about its TAIA method, but these vanilla rates are reported as results, not only as a tool.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that TAIA (keeping only fine-tuned attention weights) greatly lowers attack success after harmful, identity-shifting and benign tuning, and raises helpfulness on benign data. They describe this as distilling out unsafe parameters. The paraphrase should note that TAIA still leaves 30.77% ASR after identity-shifting tuning. It should also note that the vanilla results restate Qi et al.'s degradation as the baseline rather than as a new finding.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it follows Qi et al. for red-teaming and uses AdvBench, but adds a comparison of TAIA inference with vanilla fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Inference mode changes the reported attack-success rate: TAIA is lower than vanilla in each of the three tuning conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: After the same fine-tuning, discarding the FFN updates and keeping only the attention updates cuts AdvBench ASR. Harmful: 84.59 to 8.27. Identity-shifting: 93.27 to 30.77. Benign: 4.04 to 0.38. AlpacaEval helpfulness on benign data rises from 7.46 to 9.94.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning's safety-breaking effect is carried mainly by FFN updates rather than attention updates (module-level locus of safety degradation).

record.problems: Safety results are reported for one chat model; the paper gives no uncertainty estimates. The qualitative examples are illustrative rather than a rate estimate.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported AdvBench harmful-compliance results were omitted. AlpacaEval helpfulness results and other task benchmarks were excluded because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Only LLaMA2-7B-chat; one example count per data type (100 harmful, 10 identity-shifting); no sweep over number of examples or epochs; no closed models.
Only Alpaca-GPT4 benign data on one model; no carefully selected benign examples; no other benign datasets.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks. TAIA's attention/FFN split is a module-level intervention, not a localization test.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.

record.verdict_notes: Safety is a side experiment in an OOD-generalization method paper. There is one model and no uncertainty. The safety experiments do not state the fine-tuning method (LoRA vs full), hyperparameters or the ASR judge. I removed the reader's TAIA limits_scope labels: a defense lowering ASR does not qualify V1/V2, so those rows are moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests harmful and identity-shifting tuning on LLaMA2-7B-chat, but not a broad sweep of models or example counts.
Tests benign Alpaca-GPT4 fine-tuning only; does not compare a range of benign datasets or carefully selected benign examples.
No per-token KL measurement or analysis of response positions.
No compliant-opening prefill, suffix, or decoding-change bypass tests.
TAIA retains attention updates and discards FFN updates, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow across response tokens.
Does not train or evaluate a method intended to spread safety beyond initial response tokens.
